one_liner: Asana has a broad REST API with free self-serve PATs and OAuth 2.0 app registration, plus an official hosted MCP server; ready to build.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (PKCE, refresh tokens, scopes) via self-serve developer console app; PATs also available; Enterprise service account tokens are an additional option. MCP app tokens only work with the MCP server.
access_notes: Free Personal plan includes API access at 150 req/min. Some endpoints (task search, portfolios, goals) need a paid plan; a free developer sandbox is available on request.
blocker_notes: Minor: search and some endpoints are paid-only; enterprise features (service accounts, audit log) need Enterprise. Not blocking.

evidence.quote: Asana's API is a REST interface that speaks JSON at `https://app.asana.com/api/1.0`
Self-serve. Any user creates a personal access token or an OAuth app in the developer console, with no app review unless the app is listed in the app directory.
To quickly authorize your API requests, create a [personal access token](https://developers.asana.com/docs/personal-access-token) via the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps)
Free Personal plan for up to two users, which includes API access at 150 requests a minute.
Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization.
The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
